claims.text: Adding 1 at.% Ti to Co-free FeNiCrMn will improve its balance of strength and ductility under dynamic loading.
The proposed improvement will remain valid from -200°C to 600°C.
The proposed improvement will remain valid from strain rates of 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
Adding 1 at.% Ti will cause Ti-rich precipitates to form in FeNiCrMn.
Adding 1 at.% Ti will modify the lattice structure of FeNiCrMn.
Adding 1 at.% Ti will refine the grain structure of FeNiCrMn.
Ti-induced grain refinement will increase strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
Ti-rich precipitates will increase strength through precipitation hardening.
Ti-induced lattice modification will contribute solid-solution strengthening.
The combined strengthening mechanisms will enhance both strength and ductility.
Relative to unmodified FeNiCrMn, adding 1 at.% Ti will increase yield strength by 15%.
Relative to unmodified FeNiCrMn, adding 1 at.% Ti will increase elongation to failure by 20%.
The exact mechanisms by which Ti affects the dynamic mechanical behavior of FeNiCrMn are not fully understood.
The optimal Ti content may vary with application and testing conditions.
The hypothesis is to be tested by comparing Ti-modified and unmodified FeNiCrMn using tensile testing and dynamic mechanical analysis over multiple temperatures and strain rates.
The hypothesis is declared falsified if the Ti-modified alloy shows less than a 10% increase in yield strength and elongation to failure.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies 15% higher yield strength and 20% higher elongation, but the falsification rule only rejects improvements below 10%. Outcomes between 10% and the predicted values could contradict the quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
